SA NB 1. Reapprove the Form of the Preliminary Official Statement for the Housing Programs Refunding Bond Issue of 2017
Recommendation:

SA NB 1 attachment
On December 13, 2016, this board approved the refunding of Lancaster Redevelopment Agency Combined Redevelopment Project Areas (Housing Programs) Subordinate Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds, Issue of 2003 (the "2003 Bonds") and Combined Redevelopment Project Areas (Housing Programs) Tax Allocation Bonds, Issue of 2009 (the "2009 Bonds"), subject to subsequent approval by the Lancaster Successor Agency Oversight Board and the Department of Finance. Those approvals occurred on December 14, 2016 and February 13, 2017, respectively. This recommendation reapproves the form of the Preliminary Official Statement for the purpose of deeming it final within the meaning of Rule 15c2-12 of the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934. The resolution also appoints Nixon Peabody LLP as Bond Council and Norton Rose Fulbright US LLP as Special Tax Counsel.

CC 2. Approve the Check and Wire Registers for February 5, 2017 â€“ February 18, 2017 in the amount of $2,133,486.11.
At each regular City Council Meeting, the City Council is presented with the financial claims (invoices) against the City for purchase of materials, supplies, services, and capital projects for checks and Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments issued the prior two to three weeks. This process provides the City Council the opportunity to review the expenses of the City. The justifying backup information for each expenditure is available in the Finance Department.

CC 3. Adopt Ordinance No. 1021, (the â€œOrdinanceâ€), adding Chapter 5.60 to the Lancaster Municipal Code relating to the prohibition of nonmedical marijuana businesses.
This Ordinance prohibits to the fullest extent allowed by law nonmedical commercial recreational marijuana activities of all types including, but not limited to, the sale, transportation, distribution, cultivation, possession, manufacturing, delivery, testing, storing, labeling, and processing and personal cultivation of marijuana outdoors. This Ordinance also authorizes the City Manager to promulgate such regulations as may be necessary or convenient to implement the Ordinance, including, without limitation, reasonable regulations for the cultivation of nonmedical marijuana that occurs inside a residence or accessory structure. Any violation of this Ordinance is a misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine in an amount to be established by resolution of the City Council, or by imprisonment for a period of not more than six (6) months, or by both.

CC 4. Adopt Resolution No. 17-10, declaring its intention to summarily vacate and abandon certain offers to dedicate street rights-of-way and slope easements along 107th Street West between AvenueÂ K and Avenue K-4.
In 1982 and 1983, the County of Los Angeles (County) was offered street rights-of-way through Instrument Nos. 82-1247057, 82-1247059, and 83-1145885 recorded in the County of Los Angeles, State of California. The County also accepted slope easements alongside said street through Instrument Nos. 82-1247058, 82-1247060, and 83-1145884 recorded in the County of Los Angeles, State of California. Since such time, the City has taken jurisdiction of said properties, and has the right to accept and vacate said offers and easements. Per the Streets and Highways Code Sections 8330 to 8336, the easements can be summarily vacated if the easements have not been used, if there is not a foreseeable need, and if the easements can be considered excess and abandoned.

CC 7. Approve the Reimbursement Agreement with Viper Enterprises to facilitate development of a new dealership in the Lancaster Auto Mall and installation of high-quality improvements to the public realm; and authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute all related documents.
The proposed agreement would guarantee the launch of the RAM of the West in the Lancaster Auto Mall, thus providing the benefits of sales tax revenue, job creation and a major amenity for vehicle shoppers from throughout the region well into the future. In return, the City will provide up to $1.1 million in public improvements needed around the site of the new dealership, including street and traffic improvements on 10th Street West and Avenue K-8; landscaping and irrigation; street lighting; drainage improvements; and more.
CC 7
CC 7 attachment
CC 8. Adopt Resolution No. 17-13, approving and adopting a Debt Policy as required by Senate Bill No. 1029.
On September 12, 2016 Section 8855 of the Government Code was amended by the adoption of Senate Bill No. 1029 (SB 1029). The recently approved bill requires an issuer of debt to adopt local debt policies concerning the use of debt. Resolution 17-13, provides guidance in the issuance and management of debt by the City of Lancaster and is intended to comply with SB 1029.

NEW BUSINESS
NB 1. Approval of Conceptual Framework for Lancaster Health District
Recommendation:
Approve the proposed conceptual framework for the Lancaster Health District initiative, which aims to foster job creation and new development within the heart of Lancaster while enhancing residents' access to high-quality health care.
The overarching goal of the health district is to foster development and job creation, all while enhancing access to health care as well as retail and dining opportunities for the residents of the Antelope Valley. With over 350 acres and more than 100 of those vacant, the district represents an incredible opportunity for infill development in the heart of our city. Each new development has the power to bring new jobs for local residents, particularly in the stable and high-paying health care sector, as well as new amenities such as restaurants, shopping, and a variety of housing options in a walkable urban atmosphere.

CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING
CPH 1. Appeals of Planning Commission Decisions approving the following requests:
* Conditional Use Permit No.'s 16-02a and 16-02b, requests to construct a 50-megawatt photovoltaic solar generating facility on 307 acres in the RR-2.5 zone, generally bounded by Avenue F, 95th Street West, Avenue G, and 100th Street West; and
* Conditional Use Permit No.'s 16-07a and 16-07b, requests to construct a 15-megawatt photovoltaic solar generating facility on 177 acres in the RR-2.5 zone, generally bounded by Avenue F, 100th Street West, Avenue F-8, and 105th Street West.
Recommendations:
a.
Adopt Resolution No. 17-08, upholding the Planning Commission decision and approving Conditional Use Permit No. 16-02a and Conditional Use Permit No. 16-02b.
b.
Adopt Resolution No. 17-09, upholding the Planning Commission decision and approving Conditional Use Permit No. 16-07a and Conditional Use Permit No. 16-07b.
The Planning Commission held an initial hearing on the requested conditional use permits at their regular meeting of December 19, 2016. The Commission received a number of written and oral comments at this meeting, and continued the matter to their regular meeting of January 17, 2017, in order to allow sufficient time for review and response to the issues raised. During that meeting, the Commission heard additional testimony regarding the proposed projects, and considered the issues in light of the evidence presented. Following the hearing, the Planning Commission voted (by a 6-1 vote) to approve the conditional use permits. The Planning Commission, in its review and consideration of the testimony provided, considered the issues raised by the appellant, specifically 1) Dust; 2) Zoning, Setback and Landscaping; 3) Traffic and Roadways; 4) Cumulative Impacts; and 5) Aesthetics. Staff believes that the proposed projects are consistent with the City's zoning requirements for the site, and that the conditions of approval proposed for the projects will adequately mitigate both potential impacts during the construction phase, as well as during long-term operation of the projects.

The City Council has introduced Ordinance No. 1021(the "Ordinance"), which, if adopted, will add Chapter 5.60 to the City's Municipal Code and prohibit to the fullest extent allowed by law nonmedical commercial recreational marijuana activities of all types including, but not limited to, the sale, transportation, distribution, cultivation, possession, manufacturing, delivery, testing, storing, labeling, and processing and personal cultivation of marijuana outdoors. Any violation of the Ordinance is a misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine in an amount to be established by resolution of the City Council, or by imprisonment for a period of not more than six (6) months, or by both.
